title: The First Letter to the Thessalonians
lead: Probably the oldest surviving Christian writing, written about AD 50 by Paul with Silvanus and Timothy to a young church of former idol worshipers in Thessalonica that they had been forced to leave. It thanks God for the church's faith, love and hope, tells how the preachers lived among them, and teaches holy living, comfort about the dead, and readiness for the day of the Lord, including the passage on believers "caught up" to meet the Lord (4:17).

sections.b: A thanksgiving that keeps returning (1:2-10; 2:13; 3:9) frames the story of the church's founding (2:1-12), its persecution (2:13-16), Paul's attempts to return and Timothy's mission (2:17-3:10), and a prayer (3:11-13). The second half teaches holiness (4:1-8), love and quiet work (4:9-12), the hope for the dead (4:13-18), the day of the Lord (5:1-11) and life together in the church (5:12-28).

Nearly all scholars hold that Paul wrote the letter, and most date it about AD 49-51, while Paul was in Corinth (Acts 18), which makes it probably the earliest of his letters. Debated passages are 2:13-16, which some think was added after AD 70, and 5:1-11.
